description: UK Standard for Professional Engineering Competence defining competency standards for Chartered Engineers, Incorporated Engineers, and Engineering Technicians

CEng.title: Chartered Engineer
CEng.description: Chartered Engineers develop solutions to engineering problems using new or existing technologies, through innovation, creativity and change. They might develop and apply new technologies, promote advanced designs and design methods, introduce new and more efficient production techniques, marketing and construction concepts, pioneer new engineering services and management methods.

A.title: Use a combination of general and specialist engineering knowledge and understanding
A.full_description: Maintain and extend a sound theoretical approach to good practice in engineering, supported by a breadth and depth of knowledge and understanding from established theories, principles and best practices. Apply appropriate theoretical and practical methods to analyse and solve engineering problems. Identify and apply relevant codes of practice and industry standards.

sub_competencies.description: Have maintained and extended a sound theoretical approach to enable them to develop their particular role
evidence_examples: Formal training related to your role
Learning and developing new engineering knowledge in a different industry or role
Understanding the current and emerging technology and technical best practice in your area of expertise
Developing a broader and deeper knowledge base through research and experimentation
Learning and developing new engineering theories and techniques in the workplace

sub_competencies.description: Are developing technological solutions to unusual or challenging problems, using their knowledge and understanding and/or dealing with complex technical issues or situations with significant levels of risk.
evidence_examples: Carrying out technical research and development
Developing new designs, processes or systems based on new or evolving technology
Carrying out complex and/or non-standard technical analyses
Developing solutions involving complex or multi-disciplinary technology
Developing and evaluating continuous improvement systems
Developing solutions in safety-critical industries or applications

B.title: Apply appropriate theoretical and practical methods to design and develop engineering solutions
B.full_description: Design or develop solutions to complex problems that may not have clear answer or standard methodology. Produce designs and specifications with supporting calculations, drawings and documents. Ensure compliance with relevant codes of practice, safety and sustainability requirements. Evaluate outcomes against technical, commercial and sustainability requirements.

sub_competencies.description: Take an active role in the identification and definition of project requirements, problems and opportunities
evidence_examples: Identifying projects or technical improvements to products, processes or systems
Preparing specifications, taking account of functional and other requirements
Establishing user requirements
Reviewing specifications and tenders to identify technical issues and potential improvements
Carrying out technical risk analysis and identifying mitigation measures
Considering and implementing new and emerging technologies

sub_competencies.description: Can identify the appropriate investigations and research needed to undertake the design, development and analysis required to complete an engineering task and conduct these activities effectively
evidence_examples: Identifying and agreeing appropriate research methodologies
Investigating a technical issue, identifying potential solutions and determining the factors needed to compare them
Identifying and carrying out physical tests or trials and analysing and evaluating the results
Carrying out technical simulations or analysis

Preparing, presenting and agreeing design recommendations, with appropriate analysis of risk, and taking account of cost, quality, safety, reliability, accessibility, appearance, fitness for purpose, security (including cyber security), intellectual property constraints and opportunities, and environmental impact

sub_competencies.description: Can implement engineering tasks and evaluate the effectiveness of engineering solutions.
evidence_examples: Ensuring that the application of the design results in the appropriate practical outcome
Implementing design solutions, taking account of critical constraints, including due concern for safety, sustainability and disposal or decommissioning
Identifying and implementing lessons learned
Evaluating existing designs or processes and identifying faults or potential improvements including risk, safety and life cycle considerations
Actively learning from feedback on results to improve future design solutions and build best practice

C.title: Provide technical and commercial management
C.full_description: Plan for effective project implementation including resource allocation, scheduling and risk management. Lead or take responsibility for planning people, technical and other resources. Manage budget, programme and quality. Identify and manage commercial, contractual and legal issues. Assess and manage risks.

sub_competencies.description: Plan the work and resources needed to enable effective implementation of a significant engineering task or project
evidence_examples: Preparing budgets and associated work programmes for projects or tasks
Systematically reviewing the factors affecting the project implementation including safety, sustainability and disposal or decommissioning considerations
Carrying out a task or project risk assessment and identifying mitigation measures
Leading on preparing and agreeing implementation plans and method statements
Negotiating and agreeing arrangements with customers, colleagues, contractors and other stakeholders, including regulatory bodies
Ensuring that information flow is appropriate and effective

sub_competencies.description: Manage (organise, direct and control), programme or schedule, budget and resource elements of a significant engineering task or project
evidence_examples: Operating or defining appropriate management systems including risk registers and contingency systems
Managing the balance between quality, cost and time
Monitoring progress and associated costs and cost forecasts, taking appropriate actions when required
Establishing and maintaining appropriate quality standards within legal and statutory requirements
Interfacing effectively with customers, contractors and other stakeholders

sub_competencies.description: Lead teams or technical specialisms and assist others to meet changing technical and managerial needs
evidence_examples: Agreeing objectives and work plans with teams and individuals
Reinforcing team commitment to professional standards
Leading and supporting team and individual development
Assessing team and individual performance, and providing feedback
Seeking input from other teams or specialists where needed and managing the relationship
Providing specialist knowledge, guidance and input in your specialism to engineering teams, engineers, customers, management and relevant stakeholders
Developing and delivering a teaching module at Masters level, or leading a University research programme

sub_competencies.description: Bring about continuous quality improvement and promote best practice.
evidence_examples: Promoting quality throughout the organisation as well as its customer and supplier networks
Developing and maintaining operations to meet quality standards eg ISO 9000, EQFM
Supporting or directing project evaluation and proposing recommendations for improvement
Implementing and sharing the results of lessons learned

D.title: Communicate effectively
D.full_description: Present and discuss proposals with a wide range of stakeholders. Communicate in English with different audiences using appropriate methods including written reports, formal presentations and informal discussions. Demonstrate personal and social skills. Be aware of codes of professional conduct.

sub_competencies.description: Communicate effectively with others, at all levels, in English
evidence_examples: Preparing reports, drawings, specifications and other documentation on complex matters
Leading, chairing, contributing to and recording meetings and discussions
Exchanging information and providing advice to technical and non-technical colleagues
Engaging or interacting with professional networks

sub_competencies.description: Clearly present and discuss proposals, justifications and conclusions
evidence_examples: Contributing to scientific papers or articles as an author
Preparing and delivering presentations on strategic matters
Preparing bids, proposals or studies
Identifying, agreeing and leading work towards collective goals

sub_competencies.description: Demonstrate personal and social skills and awareness of diversity and inclusion issues.
evidence_examples: Knowing and managing own emotions, strengths and weaknesses
Being confident and flexible in dealing with new and changing interpersonal situations
Identifying, agreeing and working towards collective goals
Creating, maintaining and enhancing productive working relationships, and resolving conflicts
Being supportive of the needs and concerns of others, especially where this relates to diversity and inclusion

E.title: Demonstrate commitment to professional development
E.full_description: Undertake professional development to maintain and enhance competence. Plan own development to meet needs of current and future work requirements. Evaluate own professional development outcomes. Help others with their professional development. Demonstrate professional values and judgment.

sub_competencies.description: Understand and comply with relevant codes of conduct
evidence_examples: Demonstrating compliance with your Licensee’s Code of Professional Conduct
Identifying aspects of the Code which are particularly relevant to your role
Being aware of the legislative and regulatory frameworks relevant to your role and how they conform to them
Leading work within relevant legislation and regulatory frameworks, including social and employment legislation

sub_competencies.description: Understand the safety implications of their role and manage, apply and improve safe systems of work
evidence_examples: Identifying and taking responsibility for your own obligations and ensuring that others assume similar responsibility for health, safety and welfare issues
Ensuring that systems satisfy health, safety and welfare requirements
Developing and implementing appropriate hazard identification and risk management systems and culture
Managing, evaluating and improving these systems
Applying a sound knowledge of health and safety legislation, for example: HASAW 1974, CDM regulations, ISO 45001 and company safety policies

sub_competencies.description: Understand the principles of sustainable development and apply them in their work
evidence_examples: Operating and acting responsibly, taking account of the need to progress environmental, social and economic outcomes simultaneously
Providing products and services which maintain and enhance the quality of the environment and community, and meet financial objectives
Recognising how sustainability principles, as described in the Guidance on Sustainability on page 48, can be applied in your day-to-day work
Understanding and securing stakeholder involvement in sustainable development
Using resources efficiently and effectively in all activities
Taking action to minimise environmental impact in your area of responsibility

sub_competencies.description: Carry out and record the Continuing Professional Development (CPD) necessary to maintain and enhance competence in their own area of practice
evidence_examples: Undertaking reviews of your own development needs
Planning how to meet personal and organisational objectives
Carrying out planned and unplanned CPD activities
Maintaining evidence of competence development
Evaluating CPD outcomes against any plans made
Assisting others with their own CPD

sub_competencies.description: Understand the ethical issues that may arise in their role and carry out their responsibilities in an ethical manner.
evidence_examples: Understanding the ethical issues that you may encounter in your role
Giving an example of where you have applied ethical principles as described in the Statement of Ethical Principles on page 47
Giving an example of where you have applied or upheld ethical principles as defined by your organisation or company

1.title: Accuracy and rigour
1.description: Be aware of the limitations of their expertise and where they might seek further advice. Ensure work and the work they are responsible for is accurately and rigorously carried out. Ensure models, analyses and calculations are based on appropriate theories and assumptions. Validate them against sources of reliable data or past experience.

2.title: Sustainability and public interest
2.description: Understand their ethical responsibilities, manage risk effectively and work to appropriate codes of conduct. Have due regard for public health, safety and the environment. Demonstrate a personal  commitment to sustainable development. Undertake activities in a way that contributes to society and benefits public good.

3.title: Leadership and teamwork
3.description: Work effectively with others and lead teams. Develop business improvement strategies. Know how to work with diverse teams. Support inclusion and provide leadership.

4.title: Professional conduct
4.description: Conduct their professional activities in a way that is fair, honest, and with integrity. Avoid corrupt practices, bribery and conflicts of interest. Present themselves in a professional manner and uphold the reputation of the profession. Comply with relevant codes of conduct.

IEng.title: Incorporated Engineer
IEng.description: Incorporated Engineers maintain and manage applications of current and developing technology, and may undertake engineering design, development, manufacture, construction and operation. They are typically involved in developing, deploying and maintaining engineering systems and services within projects and programmes.

A.title: Use engineering knowledge and understanding
A.full_description: Maintain and extend sound theoretical and practical knowledge of current technologies and their application. Apply appropriate theoretical and practical methods to design, develop, manufacture, construct, commission, operate and maintain engineering products, processes, systems and services. Have an understanding of engineering principles and good practice.
indicators: Apply relevant engineering principles and knowledge
Use practical methods to solve engineering problems
Demonstrate understanding of current technology and applications
Apply codes of practice and standards

B.title: Design and develop engineering solutions
B.full_description: Design or develop maintainable engineering solutions to partially defined or complex problems. Apply engineering techniques that may extend beyond existing standards. Contribute to design solutions using processes, tools, techniques and methods appropriate to the complexity of the context.
indicators: Design practical solutions to engineering problems
Implement designs within specifications and standards

C.title: Provide technical and commercial management
C.full_description: Manage part or all of projects. Participate in management of technical activities. Contribute to project implementation activities such as resource scheduling and monitoring. Manage programme, budget, health and safety. Identify and manage risk.
indicators: Plan and manage project activities and resources
Work within budgets and quality standards

D.title: Communicate and work with others
D.full_description: Communicate technical matters to different audiences. Present technical proposals and findings. Prepare documentation and reports. Work effectively with colleagues and stakeholders. Demonstrate personal and social skills.

E.title: Undertake professional development
E.full_description: Maintain and enhance competence through continuing professional development (CPD). Keep technically up to date. Plan and record own development. Support development of others. Demonstrate commitment to professional development.

1.title: Accuracy and rigour
1.description: Identify their own areas of competence and where they need guidance. Carry out work accurately and rigorously. Ensure analyses and designs are based on sound engineering principles.

2.title: Sustainability and public interest
2.description: Understand ethical responsibilities and manage risk. Have regard for public safety and the environment. Contribute to sustainable development.

3.title: Leadership and teamwork
3.description: Work effectively with others. Participate in team activities. Support colleagues and promote good practice.

4.title: Professional conduct
4.description: Conduct activities with fairness, honesty and integrity. Comply with codes of conduct. Maintain professional reputation.

EngTech.title: Engineering Technician
EngTech.description: Engineering Technicians are involved in applying proven techniques and procedures to the solution of practical engineering problems. They carry out work which they would be expected to undertake autonomously, working under the general direction of engineers or technologists.

A.title: Use engineering knowledge and understanding
A.full_description: Apply and maintain technical and practical competences in own area of engineering practice. Apply practical engineering knowledge and understanding. Use appropriate codes of practice, standards and procedures.
indicators: Follow codes of practice and standards

B.title: Contribute to design and development
B.full_description: Contribute to design, development, manufacture, construction, installation, commissioning or operation of engineering products, processes or services. Apply practical engineering techniques and procedures. Identify where problems occur and seek assistance where needed.
indicators: Identify problems and escalate as needed

C.title: Accept responsibility for own work
C.full_description: Accept responsibility and work under direction on defined engineering activities. Organise own resources and time. Work safely and in accordance with good practice. Contribute to management activities such as cost, quality and  time.

D.title: Communicate and work with others
D.full_description: Present and discuss technical matters in English with colleagues and other stakeholders. Prepare technical reports and documentation. Work effectively with colleagues. Demonstrate personal and social skills.

E.title: Maintain and extend competence
E.full_description: Maintain and extend competence in own area of practice. Keep technically current. Undertake training and professional development. Be aware of professional responsibilities.

1.title: Accuracy and rigour
1.description: Recognize limitations of own competence and seek guidance when needed. Carry out work accurately using appropriate practices.

2.title: Sustainability and public interest
2.description: Be aware of ethical responsibilities. Work safely and with regard for public interest and the environment.

3.title: Leadership and teamwork
3.description: Work effectively with colleagues. Contribute to team objectives.

4.title: Professional conduct
4.description: Conduct work with honesty and integrity. Follow codes of conduct.
